# NCCL Log Parser – Quick Reference

This repository provides two simple Python utilities for working with NCCL AllReduce benchmark logs.

---

## Create Python environment

```
python -m venv ./parse-log-env
source ./parse-log-env/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## 1️⃣ Per‑run analysis (`nccl_log_parser.py`)

**Purpose:** Parse a single benchmark output file (e.g., an `*.out` file generated by the job) and optionally the submission script to extract performance metrics and an RDMA flag.

### Basic command
```bash
python nccl_log_parser.py <log_file> [options]
```

### Important options
| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--script <script>` | Path to the submission script. If omitted the script looks for `rfm_job.sh` next to `<log_file>`. |
| `--run-type <type>` | Value written to the **Run Type** column (default: `Baseline`; can be `Baseline`, `Ported`, or `Optimized`). |
| `--system <name>` | System identifier for the **System** column (default: `test`; can be `reference` (Kestrel), `test` (benchmarking test system), or `offered` (offered system, for acceptance testing)). |
| `--rdma-used` | Include an **RDMA invoked** column, derived from the corresponding script assumed to be in the same folder. |
| `--rdma-variable <var>` | Name of the environment variable in the script that stores the RDMA flag (default: `NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL`). |
| `--all-message-sizes` | Keep rows for **all** message sizes; otherwise only the four default sizes required for the ESIF-HPC-4 reporting sheet (i.e., `8`, `524288`, `33554432`, `4294967296`). |
| `--csv <file>` | Write the per‑run CSV to `<file>`. |
| `--output <file>` | Save an interactive Plotly HTML plot to `<file>`. |
| `--title <title>` | Title for the Plotly figure (defaults to a string based on `<log_file>`). |

### Example (required message sizes only)

This run will parse data for the message sizes of `8`, `524288`, `33554432`, and `4294967296` required for the final reporting sheet.

```bash
python nccl_log_parser.py rfm_job.out \
    --script rfm_job.sh \
    --run-type "Baseline" \
    --system "mycluster" \
    --rdma-used \
    --csv rfm_job_summary.csv
```

### Example (all message sizes + plot)

Note: returning the bandwidth and timings for all message sizes is **not** required for the final reporting sheet. This option is provided for convenience for any debugging and/or deeper inspection that the offeror may wish to pursue.

```bash
python nccl_log_parser.py rfm_job.out \
    --script rfm_job.sh \
    --rdma-used \
    --all-message-sizes \
    --csv rfm_job_summary.csv \
    --output rfm_job_plot.html
```

### Recommended workflow

#### 1. Parse NCCL performance data from individual logs

In this example, we have NCCL AllReduce performance logs (each named `rfm_job.out`) saved in separate subfolders with unique names (e.g., `example-kestrel-baseline/NCCLallreduce_e03e4791/`). We run the parsing script on each file individually and save it to a separate CSV into the new folder `parsed/` based on the parent folder name:

```bash
# Unpack example log files (there should be 12 *.out logs in total)
tar xzvf example-kestrel-logs.tar.gz

# Create output folder
mkdir -p parsed

# Parse example Baseline runs
for folder in example-kestrel-baseline/*; do
folder_basename=$(basename $folder)
python nccl_log_parser.py \
    $folder/rfm_job.out  \
    --rdma-used \
    --rdma-variable=NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL \
    --run-type Baseline \
    --system kestrel \
    --devices-per-node 4 \
    --csv parsed/$folder_basename.csv
done

# Parse example Optimized runs
for folder in example-kestrel-optimized/*; do
folder_basename=$(basename $folder)
python nccl_log_parser.py \
    $folder/rfm_job.out  \
    --rdma-used \
    --rdma-variable=NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL \
    --run-type Optimized \
    --system kestrel \
    --devices-per-node 4 \
    --csv parsed/$folder_basename.csv
done
```

As demonstrated above, note that users of this script are encouraged to process runs separately based on the `run-type` (e.g., "Baseline" vs. "Optimized"), but the resulting processed CSVs can be saved into the same folder (e.g., `parsed/`) for the next step.

#### 2. Aggregate individual run CSVs into single reporting sheet

We can then use the `aggregate_logs.py` script to calculate the median bandwidth and timing values based on the columns 'Run Type', 'RDMA invoked', 'CPU cores per rank', 'Number of Nodes', 'Message Size' from the CSVs generated in the preceding step:

```bash
python aggregate_logs.py \
    parsed/ \
    --glob "*.csv" \
    --devices-per-node 4 \
    --csv report.csv \
    --output report.html
```

The optional `--output` argument produces an interactive visualization that summarizes the median out-of-place bus bandwidth across message sizes based on the grouping described above.
